ideas.title: Winch the empty cart up the planks (project winch, next step)
ideas.goal: The player hooks the drum motor's rope to the empty cart, flips the switch and watches the rope go taut and the cart creep up the planks, or stall halfway with the brushes sparking blue; adding a pulley or greasing the axle changes which one happens. Fun because the outcome is decided by what you built, and you can fix a stall yourself.
ideas.toward: The cart's motor doing its first real work: the step right before the motor sits on the cart.
ideas.idea: physics/rope.jl (particles + reel length, already passing its check) placed in the game by the drum: a hemp rope drawn as a tube through its particles, coiling on an oak drum on the axle, a pawl that holds it. The cart's mass from its mesh volume x density, rolling on the planks by contact; Motor.step!(; τload) takes the rope's pull each step. Wide brushes (make-before-break) so a loaded motor never sits in a dead window.
ideas.form: A plugin change (irondrum + rope + cart), Jump in key to hook/unhook; a traced dusk film of the cart creeping up the planks behind a taut rope.

ideas.title: Hear the load: the commutator's crackle comes from the circuit
ideas.goal: The player listens to the motor: a light load hisses softly, a heavy one crackles harder and slower, a stall cracks on every break. You learn to tell from the sound alone whether the cart will make the hill, and to back off before it stalls.
ideas.toward: Makes the motor and later the cart readable by ear, the way a driver hears an engine labour.
ideas.idea: Each logged brush break (1/2 L I^2, now from the converged 8 mH) becomes a synthesized click: a short noise burst whose loudness follows the energy and whose spectrum follows the arc (air breakdown hiss vs copper-vapour snap above the minimum arc current). The hum underneath is the torque ripple at the real commutation rate. Nothing recorded: the sound is the circuit.
ideas.form: Audio synthesized in the game from the drum's own events, heard in the browser; a short film with sound of the motor loading up.

ideas.title: Lumi turns the brush rocker by hand (project brushes)
ideas.goal: The player, as Lumi, grips the brush holder and turns it while the motor runs: at one angle the sparks die and the motor speeds up, off it they flare blue. As the load changes the sweet spot moves, so you keep chasing it by eye and ear like an old engineman.
ideas.toward: Gets the motor's efficiency up before it has to carry three friends; the first time Lumi's hand really adjusts a machine part.
ideas.idea: Per-coil circuit branches with brush contact resistance from the overlap of a brush of real width with each segment; the shorted coil's current decays with L/R (~8 mH); armature reaction from the Newton field solve shifts the neutral with current. Lumi's beak/hand IK holds the rocker.
ideas.form: Physics in motor.jl + an interaction in Jump in; a close traced film of the rocker turning and the sparks fading.

ideas.title: Crank the drum backwards: the dynamo lights a wire
ideas.goal: The player cranks the drum motor by hand and a thin iron wire across its brushes warms to dull red, then orange; crank harder and it glows brighter, too hard and it melts through. A game of keeping it glowing without burning it.
ideas.toward: The road's 'motor run backwards' step: the same machine as a generator, the half the windmill needs.
ideas.idea: Motor.step! with the shaft driven by the crank torque instead of the pots: back-EMF becomes the source, the wire's resistance rises with temperature (Joule heating, radiation and convection loss), its glow is blackbody colour from its own temperature, and it parts at iron's melting point. The crank's resistance grows with the current, so the player feels the load.
ideas.form: A plugin interaction (crank key in Jump in), a traced dusk film of the wire glowing up as Lumi cranks faster.

ideas.title: Form the lead plates: an accumulator you have to train
ideas.goal: The player charges two lead strips in a jar of acid from the cranked dynamo, discharges them through the glowing wire, and charges again; each cycle the plates hold more, bubbles rise when they are full, and overcharging just wastes your cranking in fizz. You get better at forming them, and the battery remembers it.
ideas.toward: Planté's accumulator, the store that lets yesterday's wind drive the cart.
ideas.idea: Electrochemistry per plate: lead to PbO2 on the positive (brown), spongy lead on the negative, capacity growing with each forming cycle by the corroded depth; gassing when the plate is full (bubble particles rising); internal resistance and voltage from state of charge. The glass jar refracts the bubbles in the path tracer.
ideas.form: A new physics file + plugin by the drum's block; a traced still of fizzing plates in the jar at dusk.

ideas.title: Three ponies on the cart: weight from what they are
ideas.goal: Friends climb onto the cart one by one and the player sees it settle lower on its axles; on the winch it slows with each friend, and with the third it stalls, and one of them gets off grumbling. A comic, physical way to learn what your machine can lift.
ideas.toward: The big goal's moment (friends aboard, stops short): real masses for the friends, todo #745.
ideas.idea: Each creature's mass from its mesh volume x a body density; the cart frame's springs (or the planks' bending) take the load; the winch's stall torque decides who has to walk. Creature behaviour: a friend asked to get off picks itself by mood.
ideas.form: Creature data + a cart plugin step; a film of the cart creeping, sagging, stalling and a pony stepping off.

ideas.title: The eddy brake: a copper disc that slows the cart and fills the plates
ideas.goal: On the way down the dune the player pulls a lever that swings a copper disc between the magnet stones: the cart slows smoothly without touching anything, and with the dynamo switched in the braking charges the plates. You get to choose: brake hard and save the cart, or let it run and lose the charge.
ideas.toward: The road's last step: braking that charges the plates.
ideas.idea: Eddy currents in a spinning copper disc from the same 2D field solver (now converged): braking torque from the induced currents' Lorentz force, growing with speed; the energy goes to heat (the disc warms) or, through the dynamo coils, to charge.
ideas.form: Physics + a lever on the cart; a still of the disc between the stones, a film of the cart slowing on the slope.

ideas.title: Pitted copper: the commutator wears and Lumi files it smooth
ideas.goal: Every running hour the sparks pit the commutator a little; after a few days the motor sparks harder and runs rougher, and Lumi sits down with a file to dress it, the sparks quiet again. A daily chore with a visible result, like oiling a bike chain.
ideas.toward: Gives the motor a life across days, the daily rhythm the big goal wants.
ideas.idea: Each break's energy erodes copper at the trailing edge (arc erosion per joule), stored as a per-segment roughness map that raises contact resistance and spark energy; the file removes material where it touches, making the ring smaller. The segments' surface is drawn from the map (roughness/normal texture).
ideas.form: State that persists across sessions + a Jump in filing interaction; a macro still of a pitted and a dressed commutator side by side.

ideas.title: Reef the windmill: sail area against the gust
ideas.goal: The player sets the windmill's cloth sails, full in a calm, reefed in a gust; too much sail in a squall snaps a spar, too little charges nothing. Every windy day is a new decision, and you watch the weather to make it.
ideas.toward: The windmill that charges the plates: what the player does each day besides watching a gauge (the critic's worry about the big goal).
ideas.idea: Blade element model of the sails in the game's wind field, the rotor's torque on the dynamo through the new motor model, spar bending stress from the sail load (wood strength), the cloth's area set by reef points.
ideas.form: A windmill build + an interaction; a film of a gust coming, Lumi reefing, the sails slowing.

ideas.title: A volt-tongue: Lumi tastes the battery
ideas.goal: Lumi licks the wires to check the charge: a faint tingle, a jolt, a feather-raising zap, and its face and feathers say how full the plates are. Funny, and a real way to read the battery without a gauge.
ideas.toward: Reads the accumulator's state of charge in a way people remember, instead of a gauge panel.
ideas.idea: The current through Lumi's tongue from the circuit's real voltage and the tongue's resistance (wet tissue ~ kOhm); sensation thresholds from that current; a feather-puff and face from Lumi's feelings system, sized by the current. Lumi already has a taste_cell event: this extends it to the whole battery.
ideas.form: A Lumi body/feeling interaction; a short film of Lumi tasting the wires at three charge levels.
